editorial_note: Canto 11 data remains under full source and translation review. The Sanskrit and English records are draft material tied to the pinned source; phrase coverage and all lexical choices still require chapter-by-chapter verification.

entries.sanskrit: तेषां पारमहंस्य-चरितम् आह---त एत इति द्वभ्यम् । भगवद्-रूपं विश्वं पश्यन्तः । सद्-असद्-आत्मकं स्थूल-सूक्ष्म-रूपम् । तच् च स्वाव्यतिरेकेण पश्यन्तः ॥२२॥
word_for_word: in two verses beginning ‘these very ones’
the universe as a form of the Lord
entries.literal_english: He describes their paramahaṃsa conduct in two verses beginning ‘these very ones.’ They perceived the universe as the Lord's form. ‘Consisting of the existent and non-existent’ means having gross and subtle forms. They also perceived it as non-different from themselves.
entries.note: The pinned witness reads द्वभ्यम्; it is retained rather than silently emended to द्वाभ्याम्. Śrīdhara's ‘from themselves’ reading is not replaced by a different commentator's ‘from the Supreme Self’ reading.

entries.sanskrit: अव्याहता अप्रतिहता इष्टाभिप्रेता गतिर् येषां ते । मुक्ताः अनासक्ताः ॥२३॥
entries.literal_english: ‘Unimpeded’ means not obstructed: they are those whose movement goes wherever they desire. ‘Free’ means unattached.

entries.sanskrit: महात्मनो निमेः । वितायमानम् अनुष्ठीयमानम् । अजनाभे भारत-व्र्षे ॥२४॥
entries.literal_english: ‘Of the great-souled one’ means of Nimi. ‘Being extended’ means being performed. ‘In Ajanābha’ means in Bhārata-varṣa.
entries.note: The pinned Sanskrit has भारत-व्र्षे rather than a normalized spelling; this is not silently corrected.

entries.sanskrit: यजमानो निमिः । अग्नय आहवनीयादयः । विप्रा क्रत्विगादयः ।
word_for_word: the āhavanīya fire and the others
entries.literal_english: The sacrificer is Nimi. ‘Fires’ means the āhavanīya and other sacrificial fires; ‘brahmins’ means the officiating priests and others.
entries.note: This Śrīdhara block has no closing verse numeral in the pinned witness.

entries.sanskrit: स्व-रुचा एव रोचमानान्, न त्व् आभरणादि-प्रकाशैः । ब्रह्म-पुत्रोपमान् सनत्-कुमारादि-सदृशान् ॥२७॥
word_for_word: by the brilliance of ornaments and the like
entries.literal_english: They shone by their own radiance, not by the glitter of ornaments and the like. ‘Like sons of Brahmā’ means resembling Sanatkumāra and the others.

entries.sanskrit: परम-प्रीत्या तद्-दर्शनम् अभिनन्दति द्वाभ्याम्---मन्य इति । ननु भगवतः पार्षदानां कथम् अत्रोपलब्धिः ? तत्राह---विष्णोर् इति । विष्णु-भक्ता लोक-पावनार्थं सर्वत्र पर्यटन्तीत्य् अर्थः ॥२८॥
word_for_word: for the purification of the world
entries.literal_english: In two verses beginning ‘I think,’ he joyfully welcomes the sight of them. But how can attendants of the Lord be encountered here? The words beginning ‘of Viṣṇu’ answer: devotees of Viṣṇu travel everywhere to purify the world.

entries.sanskrit: मया दुर्लभं लब्धमहो भाग्यम् इत्य् आह---दुर्लभ इति । बहवो देहा भवन्ति येषां ते देहिनो जीवास् तेषां क्षण-भङ्गुरोऽपि मणुषो देहो दुर्लभः, परम-पुरुषार्थ-साधनत्वात् । वैकुण्ठः प्रियो येषां, वैकुण्ठस्य वा प्रियास् तेषां दर्शनम् ॥२९॥
word_for_word: those embodied beings are living creatures
the human body is hard to obtain (witness spelling retained)
because it is an instrument for the highest human end
those to whom Vaikuṇṭha is dear
entries.literal_english: With ‘rare’ he says, ‘What good fortune! I have obtained something rarely gained.’ Embodied living beings have many bodies; for them a human body, though momentary, is difficult to obtain, because it is a means to the highest human goal. The phrase can describe people to whom Vaikuṇṭha is dear or people who are dear to Vaikuṇṭha: meeting them is rarer still.
entries.note: Both grammatical interpretations of ‘Vaikuṇṭha-priya’ in Śrīdhara are retained. The Sanskrit witness spells मणुषो; it is not silently corrected.

entries.sanskrit: हे अनघाः ! निरवद्याः ! भवतो युष्मान् आत्यन्तिकं क्षेमं पृच्छामः । यतः क्षणार्ध-काल-भवोऽपि सत्-सङ्गः शेवधिर् निधिः । निधि-लाभे यथानन्दो भवति, तथात्र परमानन्द इत्य् अर्थः ॥३०॥
word_for_word: arising even in half a moment
entries.literal_english: ‘O sinless ones’ means ‘O faultless ones.’ We ask you about ultimate welfare, because even association with the good lasting half a moment is a treasure. Just as finding a treasure brings delight, so this association brings supreme joy.

entries.sanskrit: तद्-अर्थं च भागवतान् धर्मान् ब्रूत, यदि नोऽस्माकं श्रुतये श्रवणाय क्षमं योग्यं भवति । कथं-भूतान् ? यैर् धर्मैः प्रपन्नाय भक्ताय अजो हरिर् आत्मानम् अपि दास्यति, तान् ॥३१॥
word_for_word: the dharmas of the Lord's devotees
entries.literal_english: For that purpose, tell us the dharmas of the Lord's devotees, if it is fitting for us to hear them. What sort of dharmas? Those by which unborn Hari will give even himself to a surrendered devotee.

scope: Complete source-bound Śrīdhara commentary for Canto 11 Chapter 2, verses 11.2.22–11.2.31.
